kept.claim: A request that sends any non-empty totpCode together with a valid backupCode skips the password check (line 121) and then passes 2FA through the backup-code branch, so email plus one backup code is enough to log in without the password.
kept.evidence: next-auth-options.ts:121-129 checks the password only when totpCode is empty. Lines 113-119 do not stop a CAL user who has a password. The new branch at line 131 checks only the backup code and returns the user, and the TOTP check (157-189) sits in the else-if and never runs. NextAuth passes arbitrary POST fields to authorize, so email + totpCode=x + a valid backupCode logs in without the password.

kept.claim: Consuming a backup code is a non-atomic read-decrypt-modify-write, so concurrent logins with the same code all succeed and the 'single-use' guarantee is lost; concurrent use of different codes can also resurrect a consumed code (lost update).
kept.evidence: next-auth-options.ts:73-101 reads with a plain findUnique. Lines 132-156 decrypt, set backupCodes[index]=null and save with an unconditional update: no transaction, lock or CAS. The rate limit (packages/lib/rateLimit.ts:59-77) allows 10/60s per email and is off entirely when UPSTASH is not configured. updateMany with the old ciphertext in the where clause is a sound CAS, because symmetricEncrypt produces a fresh ciphertext on every call.

kept.claim: Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have backupCodes = null and there is no way to generate codes short of disabling and re-enabling 2FA; exhausted code lists (all null) are reported as IncorrectBackupCode rather than MissingBackupCodes.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] No way to generate or regenerate backup codes for existing or exhausted users

**Severity:** LOW — the feature does nothing for every user who already has 2FA, and gives a misleading error once all codes are used.

### The Problem
Codes are created only in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, and that endpoint refuses users who already have 2FA (`TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled`). The migration `20230804153419_add_backup_codes` adds a nullable column and does not backfill it. So every user who already has 2FA gets:
```ts
if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes); // line 137
```
Used codes are replaced with `null` (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and never removed. After ten uses the array is `[null x10]`, which is truthy, so the user gets `IncorrectBackupCode` ("wrong code") and not `MissingBackupCodes`.

### What happens today vs. what will break
The "Lost access" button shows for every 2FA user, but it can never work for anyone who set up 2FA before this deploy. That is the group most likely to need it. Users who use up all ten codes are told their code is wrong.

### Research
GitHub, Google and Okta all offer "Regenerate recovery codes" (which requires re-authentication) and warn when few codes are left.

### Recommendation
- Add a password-protected `/api/auth/two-factor/backup-codes/regenerate` endpoint and a settings button that shows the same backup-codes screen.
- Treat an exhausted list the same as a missing one:
```ts
if (!user.backupCodes) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);
const backupCodes: (string | null)[] = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, KEY));
if (backupCodes.every((c) => c === null)) throw new Error(ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes);
```
kept.evidence: Codes are created only in setup.ts:60-68, which rejects users who already have 2FA (:42-44). The migration does not backfill the column, so existing 2FA users hit MissingBackupCodes at next-auth-options.ts:137. Used codes are set to null and never removed, so an exhausted [null x10] array passes the truthiness check and returns IncorrectBackupCode (:144). disable.ts:54-64 behaves the same way.

kept.claim: The object URL is never revoked and backupCodes/backupCodesUrl state is never cleared on close/cancel/unmount; since the modal stays mounted for the page lifetime, the plaintext codes and blob stay in memory longer than needed.
kept.evidence: resetState (EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:71-75) does not revoke the blob URL or clear the codes. revokeObjectURL runs only at :98, and there is no unmount cleanup. The modal stays mounted (two-factor-auth.tsx:62-72), so the plaintext codes stay in memory until the page unloads. However, the <a href> is no longer rendered after reset and blob URLs cannot be listed, so reading the codes from another same-origin script is overstated.
